a15e90181e.q: What are the most important skills for children to develop before starting school, beyond literacy?
a15e90181e.a: There are five things that are more important than knowing your alphabet. These include the ability to go to the toilet independently, being able to put on a coat and get dressed, recognizing their own name, eating lunch independently, and understanding instructions. These skills are critical because they reduce the burden on teachers who manage classrooms of 30 children.

05d2b7da12.q: Why is toilet independence a critical skill for school readiness?

Accidents happen, but being able to use the toilet independently is a fundamental life skill that makes the teacher and teaching assistant's life much easier, especially with large class sizes.

3e6e52165c.q: How can parents teach children to put on their coat independently?
3e6e52165c.a: Children can lay the coat on the floor face up, put their arms in, pull their arms out, and flip it over their head. This is described as a game changer and is taught in many nurseries and schools. When teachers help 30 kids get dressed, if the children can put their own coats on, teachers only need to help zip them up or do a few buttons.

018d6f2f66.q: What is the importance of children recognizing their own written name before school?
018d6f2f66.a: It is not about spelling or writing their name, but knowing what their name looks like when written down. Children need to recognize which peg is theirs and identify their belongings like coats or school jumpers that have their names on them. They will start seeing their name written on classroom walls and helping them understand that those letters mean them.

b89ce887be.q: What strategies help children manage name recognition when they share a class with another child with the same name?

Start referencing the abbreviated name around the house so the child recognizes and knows what they're called in class. This helps them understand which version of their name they are being spoken to.
